## Campaign rules (hypothesis.md, verbatim)

### Feature screen (must match at least 2 of 4)

A company enters the list only if at least two of these four are documented on its own site, app listing, or a named public source:

| Code | Criterion | What counts as evidence |
|------|-----------|-------------------------|
| C1 | AI food scanner or photo-based meal logging | Photo or AI meal recognition in the app (plain barcode or manual logging is noted separately, it does not satisfy C1) |
| C2 | Mobile body-composition scan | Phone-camera or app-based body composition, measurements or 3D body capture |
| C3 | Wearable integrations | Named integrations or a first-party wearable with its own data platform |
| C4 | Adaptive AI coaching | Plans or coaching that change based on the user's own data, or an AI coach or assistant in the product |

Companies matching exactly one criterion are kept only when they also run a documented multi-pillar loop (training plus nutrition plus recovery or clinical support in one product) or sell body-measurement technology already. Those are marked Tier B and are a build-the-case conversation, not a drop-in fit. Everything below that bar is listed in `companies.md` as excluded, with the reason.

**C2 found at an IN company on 2026-10-02: none.** C1 moved since August: Vively now logs meals from a photo (App Store release 2.4.0, December 2024), so Vively meets C1, C3 and C4.

### Company types in scope: verdicts for companies-verified.csv (re-checked 2026-10-02)

Company types, as approved: DTC consumer apps and celebrity or expert-led subscription programs; connected-fitness hardware with an app and a data layer; metabolic health, CGM and longevity platforms; digital weight-management programs that run ongoing check-ins; B2B fitness software and member-app platforms (franchise and studio operators included when the digital layer is real); corporate wellbeing platforms and insurer-run wellness programs; elite sport and musculoskeletal measurement companies; nutrition software companies with a consumer food-logging app.

### Exclusions

- **Public health entities.** Publicly funded agencies, state and federal health services, and public research bodies. CSIRO is the clearest case: the Total Wellbeing Diet is in scope only through its commercial operator (Digital Wellness), not through CSIRO itself.
- **Gym chains with no digital layer.** A franchise or club network qualifies only if it ships its own member app with tracking or an owned digital program. Location count alone is not a qualifier.
- **Body-scanning competitors.** Advanced Health Intelligence (Perth, formerly MyFiziq), mPort (Sydney) and any company whose own product is body scanning or body measurement from images, and anything they own (Wellteq). Also gym scanner makers whose app embeds a phone scan (the Gold Coast BIA scanner maker in `banned_terms`, whose consumer app launched with MyFiziq technology).
- **Existing 3DLOOK customers**, including Erakulis, plus everything in `marketing_vb/workspace/outbound/exclusions/global-company-registry.json`.
- **Companies already worked in prior campaigns.** The Australian telehealth campaigns (2026-07-16, 2026-07-27) covered Medibank, Bupa Australia, HCF, Mosh, InstantScripts, Medmate, Qoctor, Hopstep and Amplar Health. Those and their subsidiaries stay out, which is why The Healthy Mummy (bought by Mosh in 2023) is excluded.
- **Non-Australian head office or a US parent.** New Zealand is out of scope (Femmi, Les Mills), as is a UK or US head office on an ASX listing (Physitrack, Catapult). A company bought by a US group goes with the group to `nick` (Eucalyptus to Hims & Hers). Companies that moved their head office offshore are flagged, never silently kept.
- **Medical-claims positioning.** Anything sold as a diagnostic or regulated device. FitXpress stays operational and non-diagnostic; Australian device rules turn on the claim being made, so a candidate whose positioning is diagnostic is the wrong conversation.

### Target buyer persona

**Who buys:** the owners of the app or program experience (founders and CEOs at smaller companies, product heads), the owners of the retention metric (growth, member experience, coaching), the clinical or program leads at metabolic and longevity programs, the program owners at insurer and employer wellbeing platforms, and the partnership owners at B2B platforms. Personas as approved on 2026-08-17, with two added for the partnership and wellbeing flavours the approved sub-segment already contains:

- **Founder or CEO (smaller DTC apps and scale-ups).** Owns differentiation and the retention bet. Cares about subscriber churn, LTV to CAC, app-store standing. Objection: "does a scan actually move retention?" Answer with the visible-progress argument and a scoped trial on one cohort, never a promised lift.
- **Chief Product Officer or Head of Product.** Owns the build-versus-buy call on a body-scan feature. Cares about roadmap velocity and activation. Objection: "we could build this." Answer: pre-trained models through API or SDK, no in-house computer-vision team.
- **Head of Member Engagement, Retention or Growth.** Owns the metric this moves. Cares about month 2 to 3 drop-off and check-in cadence. Objection: "will users do a scan?" Answer: two photos, under 45 seconds from the photos to structured results, shown as a 3D progress comparison.
- **Clinical or Program Lead (weight-management, metabolic and longevity programs).** Owns outcome reporting. Cares about defensible, repeatable measurement next to the waist, weight, HbA1c or lab data the program already records.
- **Wellbeing program owner (insurer and employer platforms: AIA Vitality, Springday, Sonder).** Owns participation and what the program can report. Cares about engagement between assessments and member privacy. Objection: "individual body data cannot reach the employer or the insurer's risk side." Answer: the program decides what is shown and to whom; wellness and engagement only.
- **Head of Partnerships or Integrations (B2B platforms: Hapana, VALD, Digital Wellness, Springday).** Owns which third-party capabilities the platform offers its own customers. Cares about a feature their customers will pay for and low support load. Objection: "we already integrate a scanner." Answer: a phone capture runs where there is no device, inside the platform's own app.
- **CTO or Head of Engineering (implementer, not the economic buyer).** Cares about API quality, time to integrate, and where photos live in the data flow.

**Not the buyer (FAIL for the cold send):** only people who are not at an IN company (wrong company, a previous employer matched by domain, investors, name collisions), duplicate profiles and identity collisions. Every function at an IN company has a lane (standing decision). OUT and HELD companies send nobody.

**KPIs they care about:** subscriber retention and churn across the months after sign-up; check-in completion; challenge and Round completion; app-store rating and reviews; member experience across club and home; outcome reporting at metabolic programs (waist, weight, HbA1c, labs); program participation and points engagement at AIA Vitality and Springday; features platforms can resell (Hapana, VALD).

**Likely objections and the honest answer:**
- "We already track waist, measurements or weight" (Defeat Diabetes, 12WBT, The Fast 800 if released, Digital Wellness, Vively, Springday, Xyris, Fitstop). True. The scan is a guided capture done the same way each time from the phone, returning 80+ body measurements and a 3D model alongside what members already log. Never suggest their numbers are unreliable.
- "Our members get a scan or imaging in person" (Everlab, AIA Vitality, Fernwood's HYPOXI studios, Hapana's scanner partner). That stays where it is. The phone capture is for the time between visits; there is no published comparison of FitXpress estimates with imaging or in-club scanners, and none is claimed.
- "How accurate is it?" "96-97% accuracy against expert manual measurement" describes body measurements, not body composition; or the full `accuracy-formulations.md` §1.1 sentence; repeatability as the §1.2 sentence; validation population 38-210 kg, US and Europe, "Performance outside this scope has not been characterized."
- "Where is the data, and what about Australian privacy law?" Reply with `compliance.md` §10 answers (AWS, primarily US-West-2; TLS and SSE-S3; photo deletion; outputs stored until deleted by scan ID) and the FAQ link; documents through legal@3dlook.me. Never claim compliance with Australian law (Open question 6).
- "Is it a medical device? TGA?" Only in a reply, and only the live FAQ sentence: "An independent regulatory assessment concluded that FitXpress does not meet the definition of a medical device under the UK Medical Devices Regulations 2002 (UK MDR) or the EU Medical Devices Regulation (EU MDR)." It says nothing about Australia; no TGA claim either way.
- "Our roadmap is full." API and SDK into the existing app; 2-4 weeks for a typical basic integration (a generic figure, never a promise).

### Anti-cases (where FitXpress does not fit)

- Equipment or apparel sellers with no recurring software surface.
- Content-only libraries (streamed classes with no measurement ambition).
- Clinical or diagnostic-positioned platforms (regulated-device conversation, out of scope).
- Companies whose core product is body scanning or body measurement from images (competitors and their app partners, see Exclusions). Strength, force and movement testing (VALD) is not body measurement and stays a partnership.
- Very small or unstable operations: pre-launch products, products taken off sale and apps in the middle of a shutdown or migration (Baseline by Ashy Bines on 2026-08-14; Vitruvian on 2026-10-02), and companies with no product activity for well over a year (Sleepfit, HELD).
- **Displacement:** an account that already runs a phone-camera body scan or has signed a scanning vendor is HELD for Vadim, never sent standard copy (Signos on 2026-09-29). None on this list on 2026-10-02.
- **Partial overlap, not displacement:** an account that already measures by another route (tracker, tape, scale, in-club scanner, clinic imaging) stays IN, and the pitch moves to how the capture is done and what comes with it, never to the measurement itself (9amHealth on 2026-09-29; twelve accounts here).
- **Head office or parent in the US:** the account belongs to `nick` (Centr, Perx Health, Catapult, Eucalyptus with Hims & Hers).
- **Head office unresolved between two profiles:** HELD until Vadim decides (The Fast 800: UK company and leadership against a Perth listing).

## ICP segment (icp-detail.md, verbatim)

### 8. Connected & Digital Fitness

**What they are:** connected fitness platforms, digital fitness apps, virtual personal training, wellness & coaching apps, fitness subscription platforms, AI-powered fitness tech, corporate wellness & fitness platforms.

**Buyer titles:**
- Founder / CEO
- Chief Product Officer
- Head of Growth
- VP User Engagement / VP Engagement / Retention
- CTO
- Product Manager
- Digital Experience Manager
- Fitness Program Director
- Innovation & Partnerships Team

**Company size & revenue:** Series B-public. **$1M+ annual revenue** — сильный фокус на recurring subscriptions/retention.

**Geo:** US, UK, Canada, Germany, UAE, Australia, Nordics.

**Pain points — Product & Engagement:**
- Пользователи теряют мотивацию без visible progress
- Слабый long-term retention
- Общие рекомендации, ограниченная персонализация
- Low-value методы трекинга

**Pain points — Operational & Business:**
- Сложно дифференцироваться от конкурентов
- Высокий churn после onboarding
- Растущий CAC требует более сильного engagement
- Пользователи ожидают AI-персонализацию

**KPIs:** subscription retention, daily/weekly active users, trainer-to-member ratio efficiency.

**Examples to target (verify status before outreach):** Peloton (digital), Future, Centr, Fitbod, Tonal, Freeletics, Zing Coach, Verv; Corporate Wellness: Wellhub, Virgin Pulse; Whoop (adjacent, для benchmarking).
